turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hello, Doctor. Well, I came in because... I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. It's really getting out of hand. Take my kitchen table, for instance—it is just completely covered with my husband’s appointment papers. He’s been having so much trouble with his sciatica lately, poor thing, and the doctors have him going to all these different specialists. We went to one last Tuesday—or was it Wednesday?—and the parking there was just dreadful. They charge you five dollars just to park for an hour, and the machine wouldn't even take my crisp dollar bills! 

But anyway, where was I? Oh, the table... yes. It's just buried under his papers, and then all these church flyers. I help out with the altar guild, you know, though lately I haven't been much help at all because I keep losing the schedule. And then there are the senior-center notes, and just... half-finished lists everywhere. I sit down there in the morning with my tea, trying to figure out what to do, and I just stare at the piles. I don't know which thing to pick up first or where to even begin. And then suddenly it's four o'clock and the whole day is just gone.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states she cannot get anything in order and struggles to figure out where to begin with her disorganized piles of papers and lists.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient mentions she keeps losing the schedule for the altar guild.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, going off-topic about her husband's sciatica and parking issues before catching herself and returning to the main point.

I always have a cup of Earl Grey in the morning—my daughter bought me this lovely electric kettle for my birthday last year. It heats up the water in practically seconds! Which is so much better than the old stovetop one I had. That thing used to whistle so loud it would completely startle the cat. Poor Mr. Whiskers, he’s fifteen now and getting a bit deaf anyway, but that whistle was just piercing. We had to take him to the vet just last month for his teeth, actually, which cost a small fortune... 

But, oh, what were you asking? About the table? Yes, I just look at it all and... I really couldn't tell you how I feel, to be honest. I just don't know.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality, wandering far off-topic from the original question to discuss a kettle, a cat's reaction to a whistle, and a vet bill.
